Chapter I · What Is Power Query

The engine that prepares the data

Power Query is the engine that performs ETL: pulls data from a source (Extract), cleans and shapes it (Transform), and loads it into the model (Load).

1

Almost no code

Every click generates a line of M code behind the scenes. You work with the mouse, and the code writes itself.

2

Full repeatability

You define it once. On every Refresh, all the cleaning reruns automatically on the new data.

3

Hundreds of sources

Excel, databases, websites, folders and API — and it all comes together in one place.

the moral: Power Query is the kitchen before the restaurant. You don't serve raw ingredients — first you clean, cut and arrange, and only cooked data reaches the plate, meaning the model.

Chapter I · What Is Power Query

Authentication and secure login

When connecting to a new source, Power Query asks for credentials once and saves them to the source — not to the file.

Verification typeWhen to use
AnonymousPublic sources that don't require authentication — an open website or public API
WindowsPermissions of the logged-in user — organizational network and local files
Database / BasicUsername and password — typical for SQL Server, Oracle and databases
Organizational accountAn organizational account (Microsoft / Google) in a secure sign-in window, without a password in the file
Web API / KeyAn access key attached to the request header — for API-based services
⚙

Where do you manage

File ← Options ← Data source settings. There you edit, delete or replace an expired password.

🔒

Privacy levels

Private / Organizational / Public — prevent sensitive data from leaking between sources during a merge.

⚠

Common mistake

Choosing the wrong authentication type = a connection error. Check with the system admin what the source requires.

Chapter I · What Is Power Query

An iron rule — read only

Power Query runs in an environment Read only. It pulls a copy of the data and formats it for the report — no operation here touches the source data.

✓

This screen is completely safe

Delete columns, filter rows, or replace text — no change will affect the Excel file or the SQL server. You can experiment without worry.

↧

Want to fix it from scratch?

A change meant to affect all the organization's systems must be made at the source itself — in the database or the file, not here.

Rule of thumb: Formatting for the report's sake ← Power Query. Fixing the truth ← the source.

Chapter II · The query editor

Applied Steps — the Time Machine

Power Query works like a smart macro recorder: every click is logged as a separate step. It's the complete history of the ETL process-ETL.

stepWhat it did
Source · NavigationConnecting to the source and pulling the right table
Changed TypeThe system detected and changed data types — text, integer, date
Split Column by DelimiterSplitting a column by a delimiter
Changed Type1An extra type change created automatically after the split
Added Conditional ColumnThe conditional column that was added — the currently selected step

At the top of the panel: Properties ← Name — the query name is the table name as it will appear in the data model.

Chapter II · The query editor

Four things you must know about Applied Steps

✖

No Ctrl+Z

You can't undo an action the normal way. To fix a mistake, delete the step by clicking the ✖ that appears next to it.

⚙

Editing an existing step

Some steps have a gear icon. Clicking it reopens the step dialog — to change a value without redoing everything from scratch.

⏱

time travel

Clicking on any previous step shows exactly how the data looked before the following steps were applied.

🔎

Debugging

Thanks to time travel you can debug step by step and identify exactly where the data went wrong.

when: An American-style date (MM/DD/YYYY) might be interpreted backwards — day vs. month — or throw an error.

stepWhat to click

Chapter V · Text and Cleaning

Splitting a column — seven methods

when: To split a "packed" column into multiple columns — by delimiter, number of characters, position, or transition between character types.

methodWhat it does
By DelimiterSplitting by a chosen character — comma, dash, space. The most common and useful
By Number of CharactersCutting every fixed number of characters — for segments and fixed-length codes
By PositionsSlicing at exact indices (character 3, character 8) — for a rigid structure without a delimiter
By Lowercase to UppercaseSplit at the transition from lowercase to uppercase — mountainBike ← mountain | Bike
By Uppercase to LowercaseThe opposite — transition from uppercase to lowercase: MACdonald ← MAC | donald
By Digit to Non-DigitSplit on the transition from digit to letter: 12345ABC ← 12345 | ABC
By Non-Digit to DigitSplit on the transition from letter to digit: PO9876 ← PO | 9876
example: SKU = FR-R92B-58 ← By Delimiter "-" ← FR · R92B · 58.
Chapter V · Text and Cleaning

Splitting by delimiter — step by step

stepWhat to click
1choose the the column (for example SKU)
2Home or Transform ← Split Column
3By Delimiter
4choose Custom and type -
5Split at: Each occurrence ← OK
separatorWhere you encounter it
comma ,CSV lists, "last name, first name"
colon :Times (14:30:00) or key-value (Category: Bikes)
equals =URL addresses and parameters: ProductID=5432
Semicolon ;Exports from European systems, email lists in a single cell
profit SpaceFirst and last name, breaking a sentence into words
tab TabData copied from a TXT file or an old Excel file
CustomizedAny character not in the list: hyphen, slash, underscore, or a whole word
Chapter V · Text and Cleaning

Text formatting — Format

when: Cleaning and standardizing text. One menu that consolidates seven common operations.

operationWhat it does
lowercaselowercase — for standardizing email addresses
UPPERCASEUppercase letters — for country and currency codes (USD, ILS)
Capitalize Each WordFirst letter capitalized in every word — for names and cities
TrimRemoving edge spaces only — from the start of the string and its end
CleanCleaning hidden non-printing characters (Enter, Tab) — required when importing from free text
Add PrefixFixed text before the value: 123 ← ID-123
Add SuffixFixed text after the value: liran ← liran@company.com

Why Trim is critical: the value "Apple " with a trailing space isn't identical to "Apple". In merges and relationships, that's the difference between a match and an orphan row.

Chapter VI · Adding columns

Conditional column — Conditional Column

when: IF…THEN…ELSE logic in a graphical interface — a new value based on a condition, without writing code.

stepWhat to click
1Add Column ← Conditional Column
2Type a name: Transaction classification

5Else: "small" ← OK
Chapter VI · Adding columns

The waterfall principle

when: Classifying continuous data into categories (Bucketing) — and understanding how Power Query reads the conditions.

≡

Interface instead of code

Build IF…THEN…ELSE with clicks, without writing a single line of M.

⚠

No Between

In a window there's no "between" operator. Anyone coming from SQL or Excel looks for it — and doesn't find it.

✓

The waterfall solves this

The conditions are read from top to bottom. The first one that holds decides, and a row is checked only if all the ones before it failed.

!

Order is everything

always from high to low. In reverse order, the high values would \"get caught\" early and the \"high\" would never exist.

example: List Price > 70 high · ≥50 medium · ≥30 low · otherwise very low.
Chapter VI · Adding columns

The waterfall rule — step by step

stepthe conditionwhat happens
1If > 70 ← "High price"The engine goes row by row; 70.01 and above gets "High" and doesn't check the rest
2Else If ≥ 50 ← "Medium price"We only get here if step 1 fails — that's how the range 50–70 is actually created without Between
3Else If ≥ 30 ← "Low price"Only records below 50 reach here: the condition catches 30.01–49.99
4Else ← "very low price"The safety net: everything that's left, including 0 and negatives, automatically gets this condition
example: List Price = 1431.5 ← high price · 9.5 ← very low price.
Chapter VI · Adding columns

Index Column — Index Column

when: to create a unique running identifier for each row — useful as a surrogate key, for stable sorting, or for finding duplicates.

stepWhat to click
1Add Column ← Index Column
2choose From 0 or From 1 (or Custom with your own step)
3The column is added at the end of the table and numbers the rows by their current order

Note: the index is determined by Row order at the moment of creation. If you sort before that, the numbering will change accordingly.

Chapter VII · Filtering and Types

Number filtering — Number Filters

when: To reduce rows by numeric rules — dynamically, in a way that survives data updates.

optionWhat it does
Greater / Less Than"Floor" or "ceiling": only prices ≥50, or only items cheaper than 20
Equals / Does Not EqualAn exact match to a value — for example filtering out a price of 0
BetweenHere Between does exist — in the filter tool, unlike the conditional column window
Manual marking in checkboxesConvenient, but blocks new values that come in on the next refresh

Manual selection vs. a logical condition: the checkboxes relate to values that exist now. A logical condition will keep catching new values too.

example: Between 30…70 on List Price ← only the mid-range prices.
Chapter VII · Filtering and Types

Changing data type — Change Type

when: The most important operation. A number defined as text can't be summed or averaged.

stepWhat to click
1click on The type icon (ABC / 123) to the left of the column name
2choose Whole Number (or Decimal / Text / Date)
3If you're asked — Replace current Instead of Add new step
4Now you can perform aggregations on the column
example: Order Quantity With an icon ABC (text) ← Whole Number.
Chapter VIII · Combining tables

Merge — opening the merge

when: The equivalent of JOIN or VLOOKUP. Connects Sales to Product by ProductKey.

stepWhat to click
1stand at Sales ← Home ← Merge Queries
2The Merge window opens — at the top already appears Sales
3In the dropdown menu the bottom Select the second table: Product
4Both tables are shown one above the other — ready to define the shared key
Chapter VIII · Combining tables

Merge — the shared key

when: Here you define by what The tables connect. Without it there's no merge.

stepWhat to click
1Click on a column ProductKey in the top table — it's colored
2click on ProductKey in the bottom table — is also colored
3validation: Below appears 121253 of 121253 rows matched
4Join Kind = Left Outer (default) ← OK

The match rate is the quality gauge: 121,253 out of 121,253 means every sales row found a product. A lower number signals orphaned keys or spaces in the text.

Chapter VIII · Combining tables

Merge — the new Table column

when: The merge was created, but the data is still folded inside a single column.

what happenedWhere do you see
A new column named Product was createdAt the end of the table — every cell says Table
a step was addedApplied Steps ← Merged Queries
The code written behind the scenesTable.NestedJoin(...)
What to do nowExpand to see the data — in the next step
Chapter VIII · Combining tables

Merge — Expand and pulling the columns

stepWhat to click
1Click the Expand icon (⇆) at the top of the column Product
2we choose only The columns you need — for example List Price andCategory
3Cancel the Use original column name as prefix for short names
4OK

Don't select everything. Every unnecessary column stays in memory and weighs down the model.

Chapter VIII · Combining tables

Merge — the final result

  • The Product column was replaced withReal columns.
  • Every sales row now has a category and a price — Without manual VLOOKUP.
  • On every Refresh the merge will automatically re-run on the new data.

A question worth asking: do you really need the merge? In a proper star schema, a relationship between the tables does the same job without bloating the fact table.

Chapter VIII · Combining tables

Append — concatenating queries

when: the equivalent of UNION. To chain tables with identical structure Into one long table.

stepWhat to click
1Working on the first query ← Home ← the arrow next to Append Queries
2we choose Append Queries as New — keeps the source clean and creates a third query
3we choose Two tables or Three or more and the table to concatenate
4OK — the engine concatenates them one under the other
example: Sales_Jan + Sales_Feb (date · item · quantity) ← ) → one continuous table. This is the scenario of merging monthly files.
Chapter VIII · Combining tables

The NULL mystery — Append vs. SQL

This is the first question everyone coming from SQL asks: why were columns full of nulls created?

≡

Equivalent to UNION ALL, not UNION

Append adds the all the rows one below the other, without removing duplicates.

!

Merges by name, and is case-sensitive

Unlike SQL, which joins by position, Power Query joins Solely by the column name — and case-sensitive. City and city will be considered two different columns.

gold tip: Before Append make sure the column names are 100% identical, including case and spaces. Not identical? Do a Rename to line them up before appending.

Chapter IX · Summary and Self-Check

What we learned — eight points

01

ETL before the model

Power Query pulls, cleans and loads. What reaches the model is already clean.

02

Read only

No action in the editor touches the source file or the server.

03

Applied Steps

Every click is a step. There's no Ctrl+Z — you delete a step, edit a step, and go back in time.

04

Types first

A number loaded as text can't be summed. Change Type is the first step.

05

Using Locale

An American-format date is parsed reversed without a locale setting.

06

The waterfall principle

There's no Between in a conditional column — the top-to-bottom order creates the ranges.

07

Merge vs. Append

Merge adds columns side by side (JOIN), Append adds rows below (UNION ALL).

08

The column name determines

In Append the match is by name and case-sensitive; in Merge the matched row is the quality measure.

40 questions, all on Power Query — no modeling and no DAX
Chapter IX · Summary and Self-Check

Quiz — 40 questions on Power Query

Questions and practice

One question at a time, four options, immediate feedback with an explanation. All the questions deal only with the Power Query editor.

What does Power Query do in the workflow?

explanation: This is exactly ETL: pulling from the source, transforming in the editor, and loading — all before the data leaves-Power Query.

An action you performed in the editor — how does it affect the source file?

explanation: The editor runs in a read-only environment. You can experiment without any risk to the source data.

In the Advanced Editor, M code opens. What does the structure contain let … in?

explanation: Between let and-in a step is defined after another, and each step gets a name; after in you specify which step is the query's output.

What gets generated behind the scenes with every click in the Power Query editor?

explanation: The editor is a recorder: you work with the mouse, and the M code is written on its own and can be viewed in the Advanced Editor.

What happens to the cleaning steps on every Refresh?

explanation: Define once, and the process repeats itself on every refresh.

You want another query that continues from the existing steps, and updates with them. What do you choose?

explanation: Duplicate creates a disconnected copy; Reference continues from the original query, and any change to it also flows to the new query.

You connected to a new source and were asked for credentials. Where are they saved?

explanation: The details are saved at the source level, and are managed in File ← Options ← Data source settings.

What kind of authentication suits a public source like an open website or a permission-free API?

explanation: A source that doesn't require authentication connects anonymously; Power Query remembers the choice for future connections to the same source.

Which authentication type in the editor uses the permissions of the user logged into the computer?

explanation: typical for organizational network folders and local files — Power Query authenticates using the already-logged-in username.

What is the role of Privacy Levels?

explanation: Every source is marked Private, Organizational, or Public, and that affects what's allowed to be combined.

A column has one value with empty cells below it that belong to the same group. How do you fill them in?

explanation: Fill Down copies the last non-empty value downward — a classic solution for reports exported from Excel with merged cells.

What gets recorded in the Applied Steps list?

explanation: The editor works like a recorder: every click becomes a separate step in the list.

You made a mistake. How do you undo it in the editor?

explanation: There's no regular undo. The only way is to delete the step from the list.

You want to change a value defined in a previous step, without redoing everything. What do you do?

explanation: Some steps have a gear icon that lets you edit them in place.

A column has duplicate values and you want to keep one row per value. What do you do in the editor?

explanation: The operation keeps the first occurrence of each value and removes the rest — based only on the selected columns.

Which step is almost always created automatically right after connecting to the source?

explanation: The system guesses data types for each column and records it as a step.

Why is it worth checking the automatic type-detection step?

explanation: Automatic detection is convenient, but it's a guess — so it requires verification.

A numeric column was loaded as text. What is blocked in the editor itself?

explanation: The ribbon offers operations by column type. As long as it's text, the number tools are disabled.

Where's the fastest place to change a column's data type?

explanation: The (ABC / 123) icon opens the list of all types.

The column shows 01/07/2017 and the date is parsed backward. What's the solution?

explanation: Locale tells the engine which convention to use to read the date.

The first row in the table contains the column names, but it was loaded as a data row. What do you do?

explanation: The action promotes the first row to headers and adds a step to Applied Steps. There's also a reverse action — Use Headers as First Row.

You want a column with the month name from an existing date column. What's the right way?

explanation: Work in Add Column to preserve the source column.

Why is Add Column preferred over Transform when extracting date parts?

explanation: You usually want to keep the full date alongside its parts.

Which data type suits a money column that requires precision in calculations?

explanation: It fixes four digits after the decimal point and prevents cumulative rounding errors.

Want to shorten long numbers to two digits after the decimal point. What do you use?

explanation: Round takes the desired number of digits; there's also Round Up and Round Down.

The SKU column contains FR-R92B-58 and you want to split it into three columns. What's the way?

explanation: This is the common splitting method: you choose the delimiter character and split at every occurrence of it.

The value mountainBike should split into mountain and Bike. Which method?

explanation: The split happens at the transition point from a lowercase to an uppercase letter.

When splitting a column: the value PO9876 should split into PO and 9876. Which Split Column method fits?

explanation: The split point is the transition from a letter to a digit, hence Non-Digit to Digit — without specifying a delimiter or position.

What purpose does the Trim operation serve?

explanation: The value "Apple " with a trailing space is not the same as "Apple" — and that breaks matches in a merge.

Hidden Enter and Tab characters got in from a free-text import. What cleans them up?

explanation: Clean removes non-printable characters, while Trim only handles leading/trailing spaces.

You want to merge "USA", "U.S.A" and "United States" into one value. What's the tool?

explanation: Replace every spelling with a consistent value, before the data reaches the model.

What does a conditional column enable?

explanation: A new value is set based on a condition, without writing a line of code.

Looking for a "between" operator in the conditional column window and not finding it. What's correct?

explanation: The conditions are read top to bottom, and each row is checked only if the previous ones failed — this is how a range is created.

In a conditional column in the editor — in what order should the condition rows be written?

explanation: Conditions are checked top to bottom, so in reverse order the lower condition would catch everything and the higher condition would never be met.

What's the role of the Else row at the end of the conditional column?

explanation: Without Else, rows that didn't match will get a blank value.

Where does Between exist?

explanation: Number Filters includes Between — unlike the conditional column.

What does Merge Queries do?

explanation: This is the equivalent of VLOOKUP or JOIN: the data comes alongside, as additional columns.

In the Merge window the line "121253 of 121253 rows matched" appears. What does it mean?

explanation: This is the most important quality check in a merge; a lower number indicates orphaned keys.

After a Merge, a column was created where every cell says Table. What do you do?

explanation: The data is nested inside the column until expanded, and it's recommended to bring in only the columns you actually need.

You appended two tables and columns full of null were created. Why?

explanation: Unlike SQL, which joins by position, here City and city are two different columns. Append is equivalent to UNION ALL and does not remove duplicates.

✓ The column whose name differs will be created twice, and each one will be filled with null in half the rows. This is proof that matching by name is case-sensitive.
